question: Article 34(6)(b) of Regulation (EU) 2023/11151 requires the Commission’s general review of the regulation to assess its impact on farmers, particularly smallholders, Indigenous Peoples and local communities, and the possible need for additional support. The first such review must be based on specific studies. 1.

What steps is the Commission taking to ensure that it obtains and assesses comprehensive evidence regarding this impact, including evidence from affected farmers, producer organisations, Indigenous Peoples and local communities, and what studies, consultations or data-collection exercises has the Commission commissioned or planned for this purpose?
How will it assess the costs and practical difficulties that farmers and smallholders face in complying with the regulation?
How will it ensure that this evidence is available in time to inform its review and any proposals for additional support?

Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 31 May 2023 on the making available on the Union market and the export from the Union of certain commodities and products associated with deforestation and forest degradation and repealing Regulation (EU) No 995/2010 (OJ L 150, 9.6.2023, p. 206, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1115/oj). 1
